title: What does XLS-33 specify for MPTs?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-33 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-33 specifies Multi-Purpose Tokens with issuance-level capabilities and compact holder records. [1]

An issuance identifier distinguishes the asset, while issuance flags define controls such as transfer, authorization and clawback capabilities. Holders establish the necessary ledger relationship before receiving balances. Decimal scaling is part of the asset definition, not a foreign-exchange rate. An MPT name or metadata field cannot establish reserve backing, legal redemption rights or the issuer's commercial reliability. [1]

The public XLS-33 specification describes a design, its dependencies and its intended ledger behavior. A published standard is not proof that a feature is enabled on every XRPL network. Check the target network and any associated fixes before relying on the capability. Testnet, Mainnet and development networks can support different amendment sets, and examples in a proposal are explanatory rather than records of validated transactions. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Final. [1] Author interpretation: compare the proposed use of XLS-33 with the actual network capability and preserve the resulting evidence. Keep a design reference separate from a deployment claim and from a successful transaction receipt. This article makes no fresh network-activation claim. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
